answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 40% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the shale calculation reruns each epoch, the karst weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the trellis settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 106 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 13 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
